Coding agents are powerful out of the box, but a pile of tools isn't the same as knowing your workflow. Agent skills help bridge that gap. They give your agent reusable instructions for specific tasks, like setting up a Quest build, debugging performance, or following the conventions your team already uses. The tools are still there: command line, CLI utilities, MCP servers. Skills are what tell the agent how to use them in the right way. ⚙️ And because skills can just be markdown files, they're easy to write, update, and share with your team. Learn how agent skills can level up your workflow 👉 https://bit.ly/4vZGKW1 #VR #AI #GameDev

At AWE, Meta Developer Advocate Oscar Falmer walked through what it takes to build a web app for Meta Ray-Ban Display. The short answer: less than you might think. 👓💡 Building web apps for AI glasses only requires standard HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. In other words, there's no new language to learn. During the session, he showed a step counter web app built in under five minutes with help from an AI coding agent. It pulled data from the glasses' IMU sensors and GPS, and ran on the 600×600 display. To make getting started even easier, there's now a Chrome extension that simulates the Meta Ray-Ban Display screen in your browser. That means you can preview how your app renders on the additive display, test D-pad navigation, and catch issues before you ever touch the hardware. 🚀 Watch the full session to get started 👉 https://bit.ly/44HOuA5 #AWE #MetaRayBanDisplay #WebDev #AI

Managing Meta integrations means jumping between dashboards, docs, and your IDE. Required actions live in one place. App config in another. Webhook setup requires three different surfaces. Meta Developer Tools MCP changes that. It connects AI assistants Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex directly to Meta's developer platform via the Model Context Protocol. Your agent can: • Inspect app configuration and security posture • Check required actions • Set up, test, and manage webhooks conversationally • Search Meta developer documentation in-context • Monitor API rate limits and deprecation timelines One protocol. Nine tools. Twenty-one actions. All from your IDE. Read the blog and watch the tutorial → https://bit.ly/4gzMdhN
